No JDK or JVM is bundled. Sources are compiled by the Eclipse Compiler for Java, converted to DEX by D8, and executed by Android\'s own runtime (ART) — which is why some standard-library behaviour differs from a desktop JVM.

ART mode compiles with ECJ, converts classes to DEX with D8, and runs them on Android. Optional Java SE 21 mode downloads a verified OpenJDK Mobile runtime, compiles with ECJ inside that JVM, and runs ordinary .class files without D8. It is a runtime image, not a full JDK, so javac and Android APIs are not included.
The class library available to your code is Android\'s, not Java SE. Packages such as java.awt, javax.swing and java.rmi do not exist on Android.
The Java target setting controls the source and class-file level passed to the compiler. It does not add runtime support: a language feature that needs a newer runtime still needs that runtime.
Gradle and Maven build files are read, not executed. WireDroid parses them for dependencies and source layout, then compiles with its own pipeline — no Gradle daemon runs on the device.

Returning null — consider Optional or Collections.empty*
Indexed for on List — for-each or stream()
Diamond operator <> — remove types on right
Switch with String — consider enum or Map
Test without assert — check does nothing
Thread.sleep in test — unreliable, use Awaitility
addAll after creation — pass elements in constructor
